sections.title: Absolute value · theory and guided questions

steps.title: Absolute value — rules to know
steps.intro: Absolute value is distance from zero, so it is never negative.

tables.title: Rules
head: Rule
Meaning
rows: For a negative \(x\), \(-x\) is positive. With letters the minus does not just drop off.
Bars on a product or a fraction can go on each part
Same signs: the sizes add (equal). Opposite signs: they cancel (smaller).
Opposite numbers have the same absolute value
Bars and an even power both remove the sign

tables.title: Sign clues
head: If…
then…
rows: \(b\) has the opposite sign of \(a\), and \(|b|<2|a|\)
The given does not change when you flip all signs or swap the letters
mirror test: a choice that turns into its opposite is not necessarily true

tables.title: Solving
head: Form
Solution
rows: solve both cases, then check each answer: only \(x=2\)
both sides \(\ge0\), so square both sides

tables.title: Distance tools
head: Form
Meaning
rows: the distance between \(x\) and \(a\) (\(|x+5|\): distance from \(-5\))

tips: Expression inside the bars? Calculate the whole inside first.
Right side negative or zero? Look before you solve.
Letter on the right side? Check every answer in the original equation.
Plug in? Avoid \(0\), \(1\), \(-1\) and numbers from the choices. Two choices left? Plug in again.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} a\cdot b<0 \\ a<|a| \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(a<|a|\): a number is smaller than its absolute value only when it is negative. So \(a<0\).
\(a\cdot b<0\): the product is negative, so \(a\) and \(b\) have opposite signs. \(a\) is negative, so \(b>0\).
\(b\) is positive, so \(|b|=b\) (choice 2). Choice 3 (\(b<0\)) is false.

Choices 1 and 4 compare sizes, and the givens say nothing about sizes. \(a=-2\), \(b=7\): \(|b|=7\) is bigger than \(|a|=2\), so choice 1 fails. \(a=-4\), \(b=1\): \(\left|\frac{a}{b}\right|=4\), not less than \(1\), so choice 4 fails.

steps.stem: Given: \(|x+3|=8\). Which of the following could be the value of \(x\)?
explanation: Only \(-11\) is among the choices. Check: \(|-11+3|=|-8|=8\) ✓.
Choice 3 (\(-5\)) is a trap: it is not \(5\).

steps.stem: Given: \(|x+5|<8\). Which of the following could be the value of \(x\)?
explanation: The bars are on the small side, so \(x+5\) is between \(-8\) and \(8\): \(-8<x+5<8\).
Subtract \(5\) from all three parts: \(-13<x<3\).
Only \(2\) is in this range (\(4\) and \(10\) are too big, and \(-30\) is too small). Check: \(|2+5|=7<8\) ✓.
With the distance picture: \(|x+5|=|x-(-5)|\) is the distance from \(x\) to \(-5\). Less than \(8\) from \(-5\) means from \(-13\) to \(3\).

steps.stem: Given: \(6<|x+3|\). Which of the following cannot be the value of \(x\)?
explanation: The bars are on the big side, so there are two cases. \(x+3>6\), so \(x>3\). Or \(x+3<-6\), so \(x<-9\).
\(6\) and \(8\) are greater than \(3\) ✓, and \(-10\) is less than \(-9\) ✓.
\(2\) is in neither range: \(|2+3|=5\), and \(5\) is not greater than \(6\). So \(x\) cannot be \(2\).

steps.stem: Given: \(x<0\). What is \(5+\frac{2x}{|x|}\)?
explanation: \(\frac{2x}{|x|}=\frac{2x}{-x}=-2\) for every negative \(x\).
Plugging in: \(x=-2\) gives \(5+\frac{-4}{2}=3\). The choices at \(x=-2\): \(7\), \(3\), \(-x=2\) and \(5-x=7\). Only choice 2 gives \(3\).

steps.stem: Given: \(|2x-1|=7\). Which of the following gives all the possible values of \(x\)?
explanation: Choice 1 forgets the second case. Choice 2 just flips the sign of \(4\), but the \(-1\) inside breaks that symmetry.

steps.stem: Which of the following has no solution?
explanation: Look at the right side of each one.
Choice 1: bars equal to \(0\) means the inside is \(0\): \(x=3\).
Choice 2: bars are never negative, so they are never less than \(-1\). No solution.
Choice 3: bars are always greater than \(-1\). Every \(x\) is a solution.
Choice 4: \(x=0\) gives \(|0|=0\le1\) ✓.

steps.title: Question wordings
steps.intro: Circle the question word before you read the choices. You met must, could and cannot in topic 1.

head: The question asks…
The right choice is…
How to find it
rows: break each wrong choice with one example
true for at least one allowed value
examples that work knock out the wrong choices
false for at least one allowed value
find one example where it fails
throw out the "always" and the "never" choices

tips: A choice that is never true is also "not necessarily true".
Test only allowed numbers. With absolute value, always try \(0\) and a negative number.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} |b|=a \\ b\ne a \\ 3c=a \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(a=|b|\ge0\). If \(a=0\), then \(b=0=a\), which is not allowed. So \(a>0\) and \(b=-a<0\).
\(c=\frac{a}{3}\): positive, but smaller than \(a\). So \(0<c<a\).
The order is \(b<c<a\). With numbers: \(a=3\), \(b=-3\), \(c=1\).

steps.stem: Given: \(p<q<0<r<s\). Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(|x|\) is the distance from \(0\). \(p\) and \(q\) are both negative, and \(p\) is farther left. So \(p\) is farther from \(0\): \(|q|<|p|\) always.
The other choices compare a negative number with a positive one, and the givens say nothing about that.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} d<c<b \\ |b|<|c| \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is not necessarily true?
explanation: \(c<b\), but \(|c|>|b|\). If \(c\) were \(0\) or positive, then \(b>c\ge0\) and \(|b|>|c|\). So \(c<0\).
\(d<c<0\), so \(d\) is negative too and farther from \(0\): \(|d|>|c|>|b|\). Choices 2, 3 and 4 are always true.
The sign of \(b\) is not fixed. \(c=-2\), \(d=-3\), \(b=1\): all the givens hold, and \(b=|b|\). So choice 1 (\(b\ne|b|\)) is not necessarily true.

steps.stem: \(a\) and \(b\) are integers. Given: \(2<|a+b|\). Which of the following is possible but not necessarily true?
explanation: Choice 1 is always true. Both sides of \(2<|a+b|\) are positive, so we may square: \(4<|a+b|^2=(a+b)^2\).
Choice 2 is never true: \(|a\cdot b|=|a|\cdot|b|\) always, so it is never smaller.
Choice 3 is always true: \(|3a+3b|=3|a+b|\), and \(|a+b|<3|a+b|\) because \(|a+b|>0\).
Choice 4 is sometimes true. \(a=5\), \(b=-2\) gives \(3<7\) ✓. But \(a=2\), \(b=1\) gives \(3=3\), not "less than". So it is possible but not necessarily true.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} |a|=7 \\ |b|=3 \\ |a+b|<|a-b| \end{cases}\)
What is \(|a+b|\)?
choices: It cannot be determined from the given information.
explanation: \(|a+b|<|a-b|\): in one of the two the sizes add, and in the other they cancel. The sum is the smaller one, so in the sum they cancel. So \(a\) and \(b\) have opposite signs.
Opposite signs cancel: \(|a+b|\) is the bigger size minus the smaller one: \(7-3=4\).
Choice 1 (\(10\)) is the same-signs case, which the third given rules out. Choice 3 forgets that an absolute value is never negative. Choice 4 is right only if you ignore the third given.

steps.stem:
Given: \(a^2+b^2=2ab+9\).
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: The mirror test. Swap \(a\) and \(b\): \(b^2+a^2=2ba+9\), the same given. Flip all signs: \((-a)^2+(-b)^2=2(-a)(-b)+9\), also the same given. So the mirror of every pair that fits the given also fits it.
Swap: \(a-b=3\) turns into \(b-a=3\), its opposite, so choice 1 is out. \(a>b\) turns into \(b>a\), so choice 2 is out.
Flip: \(a+b=3\) turns into \(-a-b=3\), that is \(a+b=-3\), so choice 4 is out.
\(|a-b|\) does not change in either mirror: \(|b-a|=|a-b|\) and \(|-a+b|=|a-b|\). Choice 3.
Check with algebra: \(a^2-2ab+b^2=9\), so \((a-b)^2=9\), and \(a-b=3\) or \(a-b=-3\). In both cases \(|a-b|=3\).
Choice 1 forgets the case \(-3\): \(a=0\), \(b=3\) gives \(0+9=0+9\) ✓ but \(a-b=-3\).

steps.stem: Given: \(|x+4|=3x\). Which of the following gives all the possible values of \(x\)?
explanation: Check in the original equation. \(x=2\): \(|6|=6=3\cdot2\) ✓. \(x=-1\): \(|3|=3\), but \(3\cdot(-1)=-3\) ✗.
Only \(x=2\).
Faster: the bars are never negative, so \(3x\ge0\) and \(x\ge0\). That rules out \(-1\) at once.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} 3|x|+6|y|=27 \\ x+2|y|=3 \end{cases}\)
What is \(x\)?
explanation: Divide the first equation by \(3\): \(|x|+2|y|=9\).
Subtract the second equation: \(|x|-x=9-3=6\), so \(|x|=6+x\).

steps.stem: Given: \(|x+3y|=|3x+y|\). Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: Equal absolute values: the insides are equal or opposite.
Equal: \(x+3y=3x+y\), so \(2y=2x\) and \(x=y\).
Opposite: \(x+3y=-(3x+y)\), so \(4x+4y=0\) and \(x=-y\).
In both cases \(|x|=|y|\). But \(x=y\) is not necessary: \(x=1\), \(y=-1\) gives \(|-2|=|2|\) ✓ with \(x\ne y\).

steps.stem: Given: \(11<|2x+1|<13\). Which of the following ranges is possible for \(x\)?
explanation: Positive inside: \(11<2x+1<13\). Subtract \(1\): \(10<2x<12\). Divide by \(2\): \(5<x<6\).
Only \(-7<x<-6\) is among the choices. Check \(x=-6.5\): \(|2\cdot(-6.5)+1|=|-12|=12\) ✓.
Choice 1 (\(6<x<7\)) is what you get if you add \(1\) instead of subtracting it.

steps.stem: Given: \(x+|x|<14\). What is the most precise domain for \(x\)?
explanation: Case \(x\ge0\): \(|x|=x\), so \(2x<14\) and \(x<7\). This gives \(0\le x<7\).
Case \(x<0\): \(|x|=-x\), so \(x+|x|=x-x=0\), and \(0<14\) is always true. Every negative \(x\) works.
Together: \(x<7\).
Inside first: \(3-8=-5\).
The distance of \(-5\) from zero is \(5\): \(|-5|=5\).
Choice 1 forgets the bars. An absolute value is never negative.

steps.stem: Which of the following gives all the solutions of \(|x|<3\)?
explanation: The distance of \(x\) from \(0\) is less than \(3\): \(-3<x<3\).
The ends are not included: \(|3|=3\) is not less than \(3\). So choice 2 (with \(\le\)) is wrong.

steps.stem: Given: \(|x-3|=5\). What is the sum of all the possible values of \(x\)?
Given: \(|x|=-x\). Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(|x|=-x\) holds for every negative \(x\): \(|-4|=4=-(-4)\) ✓.
It also holds for \(x=0\): \(|0|=0=-0\) ✓.
So \(x\le0\). Choice 1 (\(x<0\)) forgets the zero.

steps.stem: How many integers \(x\) satisfy \(|x-3|\le2\)?
explanation: The ends are included: \(1\), \(2\), \(3\), \(4\), \(5\). There are \(5\) integers.

steps.stem: Given: \(|3x-6|\le0\). What is \(x\)?
explanation: An absolute value is never negative. It can be at most \(0\) only if it is exactly \(0\).
Choice 4 is the trap: "\(\le0\)" includes "\(=0\)".

steps.stem: Which of the following is true for every number \(x\)?
explanation: Choice 4: an absolute value is never negative, so it is always greater than \(-1\). True for every \(x\).
The others fail for some \(x\). Choice 1: \(x=1\) gives \(0>0\) ✗. Choice 2: \(x=5\) gives \(5>5\) ✗. Choice 3: \(x=-5\) gives \(4>5\) ✗.

steps.stem: \(x\) is an integer. Given: \(|x+6|<4\). How many different values can \(x\) have?
explanation: With the distance picture: less than \(4\) from \(-6\). The ends \(-10\) and \(-2\) are not included.

steps.stem:
\(a\) is a negative number. Given:
\(\begin{cases} |a|+5=b \\ b>9 \end{cases}\)
What is the most precise range for \(a\)?
explanation: Put \(b\) into the inequality: \(|a|+5>9\), so \(|a|>4\).
\(a\) is negative, so \(|a|=-a\). Then \(-a>4\), so \(a<-4\).

Method 2 · The most precise range: \(a=-5\) works (\(b=10>9\)), so choices 2 and 3 (which leave \(-5\) out) are out. \(a=-20\) works too (\(b=25\)), so choice 4 (which stops at \(-14\)) is out. The answer is choice 1.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} m<0 \\ n>0 \end{cases}\)
What is \(|m\cdot n|\)?
explanation: \(m\cdot n\) is negative (negative times positive), so \(|m\cdot n|=-m\cdot n\).
Choice 1: \(m<0\), so \(|m|=-m\), and \(n\cdot|m|=n\cdot(-m)=-m\cdot n\). A match.
Or plug in \(m=-2\), \(n=3\): \(|m\cdot n|=6\). Choice 1: \(3\cdot2=6\) ✓. Choice 2: \(-2\cdot3=-6\). Choice 3: \(-6\). Choice 4: \(-3\cdot2=-6\).
Check with a number: \(x=5\) gives \(|-3|+5=8\), and \(2\cdot5-2=8\) ✓. Choice 1 comes from the mistake \(|2-x|=2-x\).

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} d\ne0 \\ |c+d|=|c-d| \end{cases}\)
What is \(c\)?
explanation: Equal absolute values: the insides are equal or opposite.
Equal: \(c+d=c-d\), so \(2d=0\) and \(d=0\). Not allowed, because \(d\ne0\).
Opposite: \(c+d=-(c-d)=-c+d\), so \(2c=0\) and \(c=0\).

steps.stem: Given: \(|a+b|=|a-b|\). What is \(a\cdot b\)?
choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: Both sides are zero or positive, so we may square both sides: \((a+b)^2=(a-b)^2\).
Expand: \(a^2+2ab+b^2=a^2-2ab+b^2\), so \(4ab=0\) and \(a\cdot b=0\).

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} |x|\ne x \\ |-5x|\ne-5x \end{cases}\)
What is \(x\)?
explanation: \(|x|\ne x\) only when \(x<0\).
No number is both negative and positive. No number satisfies the conditions.
For example, \(x=-\frac15\) gives \(-5x=1\) and \(|1|=1\), so the second condition fails.

steps.stem: Given: \((a-b)^2<4\). Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \((a-b)^2=|a-b|^2\). Both sides of \(|a-b|^2<4\) are zero or positive, so take the root: \(|a-b|<2\).
The sum \(a+b\) can be anything. \(a=b=100\): \((a-b)^2=0<4\), but \((a+b)^2=40{,}000\), so choice 3 fails. \(a=b=0\): \((a+b)^2=0\), so choice 4 fails.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} |x|=-x \\ |y|=y \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(|x|=-x\), so \(x\le0\). \(|y|=y\), so \(y\ge0\). Therefore \(x\le0\le y\), and \(x\le y\).
The zero is the trap. \(x=y=0\) satisfies both givens. Then \(x<y\) fails, and \(x\cdot y=0\) is not negative.

steps.stem: Given: \(|x+2|<|x-2|\). Which of the following numbers satisfies the inequality?
explanation: \(|x+2|=|x-(-2)|\) is the distance from \(x\) to \(-2\). \(|x-2|\) is the distance from \(x\) to \(2\).
So \(x\) is closer to \(-2\) than to \(2\). The point in the middle is \(0\), so \(x<0\).
The others fail: \(x=0\) gives \(2<2\) ✗. \(x=2\) gives \(4<0\) ✗. \(x=\frac12\) gives \(2.5<1.5\) ✗.

steps.stem: What is the smallest possible value of \(|x-3|+|x-5|\)?
explanation: \(|x-3|\) is the distance from \(x\) to \(3\), and \(|x-5|\) is the distance from \(x\) to \(5\).
If \(x\) is between \(3\) and \(5\), the two distances add up to the gap from \(3\) to \(5\), which is \(2\). For example, \(x=4\): \(1+1=2\).
If \(x\) is outside, the sum is bigger. For example, \(x=6\): \(3+1=4\). So the smallest value is \(2\).

steps.stem: Given: \(|x-2|=2x+1\). Which of the following gives all the possible values of \(x\)?
explanation: Check \(x=-3\): \(|-5|=5\), but \(2\cdot(-3)+1=-5\) ✗. A fake solution.
Check \(x=\frac13\): \(\left|\frac13-2\right|=\frac53\) and \(\frac23+1=\frac53\) ✓.
Faster: the right side cannot be negative, so \(2x+1\ge0\) and \(x\ge-\frac12\). That rules out \(-3\).

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} |4x+2|=10 \\ |2x+1|=-2x-1 \end{cases}\)
What is \(x\)?
explanation: Second equation: the right side is \(-(2x+1)\). \(|A|=-A\) only when \(A\le0\). So \(2x+1\le0\), and \(x\le-\frac12\).

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} x<-2 \\ |x|=|y| \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(x<-2\), so \(|x|>2\). Then \(|y|=|x|>2\), and \(y^2=|y|^2>4\). Choice 1 is always true.
\(y\) can be \(x\) or \(-x\). Take \(x=-3\).
\(y=-3\): then \(y<-2\) (choice 2 fails), and \(x+y=-6\) (choice 3 fails).
\(y=3\): then \(\frac{x}{y}=-1\) (choice 4 fails).

steps.stem: \(x\) is an integer. Given: \(|x-1|+|x-7|=6\). How many different values can \(x\) have?
explanation: \(|x-1|\) is the distance from \(x\) to \(1\), and \(|x-7|\) is the distance from \(x\) to \(7\).
The gap from \(1\) to \(7\) is \(6\). For every \(x\) from \(1\) to \(7\) (ends included), the two distances add up to exactly \(6\). For example, \(x=3\): \(2+4=6\) ✓.
Outside, the sum is more than \(6\). For example, \(x=8\): \(7+1=8\).
The integers from \(1\) to \(7\): \(7\) values. Choice 1 counts only the two ends.

steps.stem: Given: \(b^m\ne|b|^m\), where \(m\) is an integer. Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: If \(b\ge0\), then \(|b|=b\) and the two powers are equal. So \(b<0\).
If \(b<0\) and \(m\) is even, the even power hides the sign: \((-2)^2=4=|-2|^2\). So \(m\) is odd.
Check: \(b=-2\), \(m=3\): \((-2)^3=-8\), but \(|-2|^3=8\) ✓. Choice 1 is not necessary: here \(m=3\) is positive.

steps.stem: In which of the following cases is \(|c|+|d|=|c+d|\) not necessarily true?
explanation: \(|c+d|=|c|+|d|\) when \(c\) and \(d\) do not have opposite signs.
Both positive ✓, both negative ✓, one of them \(0\) ✓. In these cases it is always true.
"Integers" says nothing about the signs: \(c=3\), \(d=-4\) gives \(|3|+|-4|=7\), but \(|3+(-4)|=1\). So choice 3.

steps.stem:
\(a\) and \(b\) are numbers different from \(0\).
Given: \(|a-b|=|a|+|b|\).
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(a-b=a+(-b)\). The sizes add, so \(a\) and \(-b\) have the same sign.
So \(a\) and \(b\) have opposite signs, and \(a\cdot b<0\) (choice 3).
The others are not necessary. \(a=2\), \(b=-5\): \(|7|=7=2+5\) ✓, but \(|a|<|b|\) (choice 2 fails) and \(a+b=-3\) (choice 4 fails).

Method 2 · Mirror test: swap \(a\) and \(b\). \(|b-a|=|b|+|a|\) is the same given. Choice 1 (\(a>b\)) turns into \(b>a\), and choice 2 (\(|a|>|b|\)) turns into \(|b|>|a|\). Both turn into their opposites, so they are out.
Flip all signs: \(|-a+b|=|-a|+|-b|\) is the same given too. Choice 4 (\(a+b>0\)) turns into \(a+b<0\), so it is out. Only choice 3 is left, with no numbers at all.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} a\ne b \\ a-b=|a+b| \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: Either way, \(a=0\) or \(b=0\).
Check: \(a=5\), \(b=0\): \(5-0=5=|5|\) ✓. This example also rules out choices 1, 3 and 4.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} P\cdot Q<0 \\ \frac{P}{Q}<\frac{Q}{P} \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: Move everything to one side: \(\frac{P}{Q}-\frac{Q}{P}<0\), so \(\frac{P^2-Q^2}{P\cdot Q}<0\).
The bottom \(P\cdot Q\) is negative. A fraction with a negative bottom is negative only when its top is positive: \(P^2-Q^2>0\).
So \(P^2>Q^2\), which means \(|P|>|Q|\).
Choices 2 to 4 are not necessary. \(P=-3\), \(Q=1\): \(-3<-\frac13\) ✓, but \(Q<0<P\) fails, and \(P+Q=-2\) (choice 3 fails). \(P=3\), \(Q=-1\): \(-3<-\frac13\) ✓, and \(P+Q=2\) (choice 4 fails).
Method 2 · Mirror test: flip all signs. \((-P)(-Q)=P\cdot Q\) and \(\frac{-P}{-Q}=\frac PQ\), so the given stays the same.

Choice 2 (\(Q<0<P\)) turns into \(P<0<Q\), choice 3 (\(0<P+Q\)) into \(P+Q<0\), and choice 4 into \(0<P+Q\). All three turn into their opposites, so they are out. Choice 1 (\(|Q|<|P|\)) does not change: it is the answer.

steps.stem: Given: \(p<q<|p\cdot q\cdot r|<r\). Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(|p\cdot q\cdot r|\ge0\) and \(|p\cdot q\cdot r|<r\), so \(r>0\) and \(|r|=r\).
\(|p\cdot q\cdot r|=|p\cdot q|\cdot r<r\). Divide by the positive \(r\): \(|p\cdot q|<1\).
The others are not necessary. \(p=-0.9\), \(q=-0.5\), \(r=0.3\): \(|p\cdot q\cdot r|=0.135\), and \(-0.9<-0.5<0.135<0.3\). Here \(r<1\) (choice 2 fails) and \(|p|>|r|\) (choice 3 fails).
